newsitem.title: UK: LME copper maintains equilibrium ahead of holiday.
newsitem.headline: LME copper maintains equilibrium ahead of holiday.

text.p: Copper prices settled unchanged on Friday notwithstanding a rise in London Metal Exchange (LME) stocks and news that a strike at Chile's Escondida mine ended.
The other base metals were mixed, with zinc and lead edging lower while nickel motored above $7,400. Aluminum was tightly rangebound.
Volumes were generally light ahead of a U.K. holiday weekend. The London market will reopen on Tuesday, May 6.
Three months copper settled unchanged from Thursday's kerb close at $2,360 per tonne, in the top end of the day's $34 range.
Prices had initially slid to a low of $2,336 in the morning after LME stock data showed an increase of 2,175 tonnes. But a light speculative buying lifted values off their lows in the official ring.
"A little shortcovering lifted prices in the afternoon kerb. Volumes have been light all day," a trader said.
But copper came off its highs following news in the afternoon that the 350-member union at Chile's Escondida mine had voted to end their strike and would return to work as of Friday.
A mine spokesman had no comment and said Escondida had not received any official notification that the two-week-old strike was over.
Escondida mangement has said previously that the strike has had no effect on production.
The copper market was still keeping a close eye on another strike in Chile at the 75,000-tonne Quebrada Blanca mine.
Aluminium was just easier at $1,624, down $4, after shadowing copper lower early in the day and then staging a slight recovery.
A stock decline of 2,200 tonnes offered little in the way of upwards momentum and trader said the market was technically driven.
Nickel was more buoyant, ending $80 stronger at $7,430, but it was still well within recent ranges.
Tin similarly was up $30 at $5,740, but failed to break fresh ground.
Zinc and lead, however, languished in slightly lower levels for most of the day and finished easier.
Zinc was $7 lower at $1,262, after probing support at $1,255. Lead, meanwhile, was $3 down at $623 after trading in a tight $5 range.
Alloy was indicated at $1,495/50, down from $1,505. --Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
